primary_variables.matched_definition: Clinical comparison between responders, nonresponders, resistant, relapsed, sensitive, or remission states.
evidence: An initial discovery cohort (n = 21) were divided into chemoresistant and chemosensitive groups and evaluated using discovery mass-spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics.
Patients were classified according to their treatment-free interval to platinum (TFIp) into two main groups: TFIp < 6 months (chemoresistant) and TFIp > 6 months (chemosensitive).

we limited our predictive analysis to two groups based on the TFIp cut-off of 6 months and therefore divided our verification cohort into chemoresistant (TFIp < 6 months) (n = 25) and chemosensitive (TFIp > 6 months) (n = 63) groups
treatment with primary surgery and six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy
predict response to first-line treatment in patients with newly diagnosed HGSC
identify proteins that differed in abundance in relation to the patients’ response to chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel

timepoints: at the time of cancer diagnosis

evidence: divided into chemoresistant and chemosensitive groups
Changes in protein abundance between groups were compared using two-sided t test analysis

base_candidates_ranked.reason: The discovery cohort used discovery MS-based proteomics with peptide areas obtained via 'Precursor Ions Area Detector' and protein abundance estimated from the three most intense peptides, which is characteristic of label-free quantification (LFQ) in DDA mode.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: The verification cohort explicitly used Parallel Reaction Monitoring (PRM) with isotopically-labelled internal standard peptides for targeted quantification.
